name: Skagit River (Upper)
blurb: Dam-fed, glacier-green water below the North Cascades Highway — Seattle City Light releases keep it floatable all summer.

sections.notes: S-Bends (Class III, AW mile ~5.8) is the main rapid. Very cold water. Copper Creek parking is limited — leave room for outfitter buses. No fee: NPS says there is no fee to raft the Skagit in a personal raft (https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/rafting-in-the-north-cascades.htm).

putInAccess.operator: National Park Service (Ross Lake National Recreation Area, North Cascades NP Service Complex)
putInAccess.sourceName: NPS Public POIs, 'Goodell Creek Raft Launch' (OBJECTID 33925, type Boat Launch; map label 'Goodell Creek Boat Launch'; digitized from 2013 NAIP)
putInAccess.note: Batch 3. Coordinate is NPS's own POI for the launch. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch3/goodell.png) puts it at a small beach clearing at the water's edge. Legal access: the NPS rafting page (https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/rafting-in-the-north-cascades.htm) says 'The Skagit River is accessible via a boat launch near Goodell Creek Campground at mile post 119 on State Route 20'.
putInAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
putInAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~236), the launch is right of the NHD centreline (~65 m; artificial path). Confirmed on imagery.

takeOutAccess.operator: National Park Service (Ross Lake National Recreation Area, North Cascades NP Service Complex)
takeOutAccess.sourceName: NPS Public POIs, 'Copper Creek Raft Take-out/Launch' (OBJECTID 20467, type Boat Launch, Ross Lake NRA)
takeOutAccess.note: Batch 3. Coordinate is NPS's own POI for the raft take-out, 27 m from the v1/AW candidate. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch3/copper.png) puts it on the north bank under trees about 9 m from the water's edge. NPS lists its XY accuracy as 'Unknown'. Legal access: the NPS rafting page (https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/rafting-in-the-north-cascades.htm) says the Skagit is accessible 'via ... the Copper Creek Take-Out near mile post 112' on SR 20; NPS says there is no fee to raft the Skagit in a personal raft.
takeOutAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~271, west), the take-out is on the north bank, right of the NHD centreline (~60 m; ftype 558 artificial path through the wide channel). Confirmed on imagery.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

mapAuditNote: Audited 2026-10-25 (final run). Both endpoints are verified from NPS Public POIs (Goodell Creek Raft Launch 33925, Copper Creek Raft Take-out/Launch 20467) plus the NPS North Cascades rafting page, checked on Esri imagery. Banks come from NHDPlus HR. No fee for personal rafts (NPS).
